sources.title: Palmer, ed.: The Languages and Linguistics of the New Guinea Area
sources.note: Academic overview of more than forty language families, isolates, regional histories, and contact.

sources.title: Foley: The Languages of New Guinea
sources.note: Peer-reviewed synthesis of extraordinary diversity, multiple families and isolates, and long-term convergence.

sources.title: Schapper: The arbitrariness of isolate classifications in New Guinea
sources.note: Explains uncertainty in boundaries between language isolates and small families.

sources.title: Lindström and colleagues: The languages of Island Melanesia
sources.note: Academic account of Papuan and Oceanic languages, contact, and competing island histories.

sources.title: Terrill: Central Solomon languages
sources.note: Shows a heterogeneous, negatively defined regional grouping with uncertain relationships.

sources.title: Max Planck DOBES Morehead language documentation project
sources.note: Community-linked documentation of two southern New Guinea languages from different Yam subgroups.

sources.title: PNG National Research Institute: Indigenous languages need protection
sources.note: PNG-authored discussion of language diversity, intergenerational learning, shift, and preservation.

sources.title: Gaffney and Tolla: The human histories of West New Guinea
sources.note: Regional synthesis stressing diversity, movement, colonial boundary-making, and large research gaps.

sources.title: Lynch, Ross, and Crowley: History of Papuan and Australian languages
sources.note: Open-access linguistic history explaining that Papuan is a cover term for many languages.

sources.title: Lilley: Papua New Guinea human past, the evidence of archaeology
sources.note: Archaeological synthesis stressing how sparse and uneven the evidence for past lifeways remains.

sources.title: Denham: Roots of agriculture and arboriculture in New Guinea
sources.note: Rejects one-dimensional stories and emphasizes regional interaction and changing local practices.

sources.title: Beer: Clan and family transformations among the Wampar
sources.note: Later local study showing that kinship terms and family forms change historically rather than forming one timeless model.

sources.title: Cámara-Leret and Dennehy: Indigenous knowledge of New Guinea useful plants
sources.note: Large review of locally varied plant knowledge, including foods, medicines, fibers, and documentation gaps.

sources.title: UNESCO decision inscribing Kuk Early Agricultural Site
sources.note: Institutional synthesis of long-term cultivation, ditches, wooden tools, and continuing land use.

sources.title: Liu and colleagues: Coastal Papua New Guinea over 2,500 years
sources.note: Archaeology and genomics of intensive southern coastal settlements, pottery, tools, and wide interaction.

sources.title: Bayliss-Smith, Golson, and Hughes: Kuk Phase 4 channels and fields
sources.note: Broadly dated wetland drainage and fields overlapping the target centuries; not household plumbing.

sources.title: Gaffney and colleagues: Earliest pottery on New Guinea mainland
sources.note: Highland pottery, axes, slate tools, local manufacture, and inland-coastal connections.

sources.title: David and colleagues: The Emo site, Gulf Province
sources.note: New excavation and AMS dating reassess claimed early pottery and later hiri antecedents.

sources.title: Skelly and colleagues: Late Lapita seafaring networks at Giligilina
sources.note: A small stratified pottery assemblage dated 2660 to 2420 cal BP supports earlier south-coast seafaring connections.

sources.title: Bonnat, Torrence, and White: Landscapes of exchange in Willaumez
sources.note: Sourced obsidian and dated volcanic layers show changing exchange, land use, and resilience.

sources.title: Shaw and colleagues: Cultural identities in the Massim islands
sources.note: Excavated sequence and pottery show long local diversification before historically known exchange systems.

sources.title: Gaffney and Tanudirjo: Raja Ampat potting traditions, 3500 to 1000 BP
sources.note: Pottery sequence bracketing the target interval in far western New Guinea islands.

sources.title: Field and colleagues: Kaironk Valley pestle starch and usewear
sources.note: Microscopic residues and wear connect a particular stone tool with plant processing.

sources.title: Mene, Setiawan, and Gaffney: Andarewa Cave occupation
sources.note: West Papuan fieldwork presents a long local sequence and explicit preservation limits.

sources.title: Tolla and colleagues: Late Holocene diets in lowland West New Guinea
sources.note: Isotope evidence shows individual dietary variation and the need for local interpretation.

sources.title: Fairyo: Decorated pottery from Kayu Batu, Jayapura
sources.note: Papuan-authored pottery study that explicitly identifies unresolved chronology.

sources.title: Barker and colleagues: Walufeni Cave marine shell and Kasua histories
sources.note: Community-linked archaeology uses inland marine shell to examine interaction across ecological distance.

sources.title: David and colleagues: Port Moresby and Southern Lowlands archaeology
sources.note: Open-access synthesis of pottery, postholes, burials, foods, settlement, and local research history.

sources.title: Kinaston and colleagues: South New Guinea oral and physiological health
sources.note: Bioarchaeological comparison shows different health patterns at two later south-coast sites.

sources.title: Koungoulos and colleagues: Environmental context of the Aitape Skull
sources.note: Reassessment of rare coastal human remains illustrates hazards and diagnostic uncertainty.

sources.title: Leavesley and colleagues: Kastom, community, education, and archaeology
sources.note: PNG heritage practitioners argue for Indigenous perspectives, oral traditions, exchange protocols, and community benefit.

sources.title: Urwin and colleagues: Agency in hiri exchange relationships
sources.note: Papuan Gulf oral traditions highlight reciprocal partnerships and challenge passive-recipient models.

sources.title: John Waiko: Be jijimo, Binandere history according to tradition
sources.note: Indigenous Papuan scholarship on oral genres, generational transmission, history, and colonial pressure.

sources.title: PNG Journal of Education: Indigenous knowledge and conservation education
sources.note: Modern community instructors and children describe guided learning of language, crafts, tools, and building.

sources.title: UNESCO: Toare Gulf mask festival safeguarding project
sources.note: Named community and PNG institutions document living songs, dances, masks, materials, and ancestral meanings.

sources.title: SIL/ANU archive: Writing New Guinea languages
sources.note: Bibliographic record for the study identifying a missionary-made Motu orthography and 1877 school publication.

sources.title: National Archives of Australia: PNG records, 1883 to 1942
sources.note: Official chronology of German, British, and Australian administrations, with an archival language warning.

sources.title: United Nations Treaty Collection: 1962 West New Guinea agreement
sources.note: Canonical record of the Netherlands-Indonesia agreement and United Nations transitional administration.

sources.title: Constitution of Papua New Guinea
sources.note: Papua New Guineans honor ancestors, customary wisdom, community interdependence, diversity, and future generations.

sources.title: PNG NRI: Strategies to preserve and reclaim cultural artefacts
sources.note: PNG-authored account of removal, repatriation, museums, cultural diversity, and youth access.

proposedOverrides.name: Papuan Language Regions
proposedOverrides.summary: A geographic umbrella for diverse language communities around New Guinea and neighboring islands, not one polity, people, ancestry, or language family.
